I am old now, sixty-five years, and this small plot near my house is where I plant my yams and cassava like my father taught me. I have no money to waste on chemical fertilizer for this small piece of land, but I will carry manure from my goats and spread it on the mounds. My sons and their wives will help me with the clearing and mounding, and during harvest I will call one or two young men from the village to help me lift the yams because my back is not strong anymore.
